status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should provide meaningful information making stakeholders aware of interactions with AI, including workplace interactions.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Section 1.3(ii) concerns awareness of interaction with AI. The documented pathway is synthetic ads/endorsements followed by human scripted calls, not a recipient interaction with an AI participant. Content authenticity is independently assessed without substituting it for interaction disclosure.

review.reason_for_change: Section 1.3(ii) concerns information before or during interaction with AI. Victims viewed static advertisements and dealt with human scammers. No interaction with the generation system or autonomous AI interlocutor is established.

review.requirement_proposition: Protect vulnerable users, require specific consent for bounded deceptive styles, document emergent deception and define safeguard-failure protocols.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: ASIC reports FY2026 AI-assisted public-figure investment scams and losses, without identifying every generating system or scam date. For IEEE-7014.1 6.7.3(l-p), the missing applicability fact is whether the operator adopted IEEE 7014.1 for an emulated-empathy GPAI partner in the interaction and the applicable vulnerable-user or deceptive-style safeguard context; impersonation imagery or task deception alone does not establish a human–AI partnering undertaking. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: 6.7.3(l-p) concerns emulated-empathy partner safeguards or emotional-data consent. Static advertisements and human-directed contact do not identify that object.

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: ASIC described deliberate AI-generated public-figure impersonations used to induce investment transfers. The portrayed figures did not provide the claimed endorsements. The AI-mediated identity use did not respect their dignity and autonomy. The result is Not aligned for the regulator-described use. Reported losses and takedown totals are distinct aggregates.

review.requirement_proposition: Add intended purpose, nominal operator and responsible contact information to the public documentation.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: IEEE 7001 Table 2 level 3 governs autonomous-system public transparency. The recipient path consists of static synthetic endorsements, human-scripted calls and scam investment platforms, without a described autonomous AI participant. The synthetic-content provenance question is distinct.

review.reason_for_change: Table 2 level 3 concerns autonomous-system identification or public system documentation. A human-directed static advertisement and follow-up are not an established autonomous AI participant.

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must ensure adequate transparency requirements tailored to the context and risk of AI lifecycle activities, including identification of AI-generated content.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 8 addresses Parties and their territorial implementation. The Australian scam record does not establish treaty entry into force or implementation covering these actors. The regulator’s warning does not itself establish that treaty duty.

review.reason_for_change: Article 8 concerns treaty Party implementation. No relevant commenced Party implementation duty is established for these US/Australian scammers or platforms.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not apply affective modeling to identifiable subject data without prior informed consent.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: ASIC reports FY2026 AI-assisted public-figure investment scams and losses, without identifying every generating system or scam date. For IEEE-7014 4.3.5.2(d), the missing applicability fact is whether the developer undertook IEEE 7014 for an emulated-empathy system applying affective modelling to identifiable subject affective data; image depiction, face swapping or identity matching does not by itself establish affective modelling, and the anonymous-data exception cannot be resolved without that processing scope. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: 4.3.5.2(d) concerns affective modelling. Cloning a professional or public-figure likeness does not identify modelling that person’s emotions.

review.requirement_proposition: Make the system clearly identifiable as autonomous to users and bystanders.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: IEEE 7001 Table 2 level 1 governs autonomous-system public transparency. The recipient path consists of static synthetic endorsements, human-scripted calls and scam investment platforms, without a described autonomous AI participant. The synthetic-content provenance question is distinct.

review.reason_for_change: Table 2 level 1 concerns autonomous-system identification or public system documentation. A human-directed static advertisement and follow-up are not an established autonomous AI participant.

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must seek to ensure that people interacting with AI are told they are interacting with a system rather than a human, as appropriate to the context.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 15(2) addresses Parties and their territorial implementation. The Australian scam record does not establish treaty entry into force or implementation covering these actors. The regulator’s warning does not itself establish that treaty duty.

review.reason_for_change: Article 15(2) concerns treaty Party implementation. No relevant commenced Party implementation duty is established for these US/Australian scammers or platforms.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not place, put into service or use AI that deploys subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques causing materially distorted behavior and significant harm.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: ASIC reports AI-assisted investment impersonation scams and Australian losses during FY2026, but the record does not identify the specific AI system or establish an EU-market provider, Union-established deployer, or output used in the Union. The reported harm does not resolve the Article 2 scope facts.

review.reason_for_change: Article 5(1)(a) requires covered territorial AI use and the defined manipulation/vulnerability harm conditions. The Bronx scam or Australian public-figure scam reports do not establish Union scope. No EU prohibition finding is inferred from fraud reports.

review.requirement_proposition: Minimise data and make review, modification and withdrawal of consent immediate and accessible.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: ASIC reports FY2026 AI-assisted public-figure investment scams and losses, without identifying every generating system or scam date. For IEEE-7014.1 6.22.3(a-b), the missing applicability fact is whether the developer or platform operator adopted IEEE 7014.1 for a partner-based GPAI system using emulated empathy and collecting personal, emotional, memory or relationship-history data in this occurrence; public output or stored task content alone does not establish that partnering and consent-control scope. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: 6.22.3(a-b) concerns emulated-empathy partner safeguards or emotional-data consent. Static advertisements and human-directed contact do not identify that object.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not exploit vulnerabilities due to age, disability or social or economic situation through AI in a way likely to distort behavior and cause significant harm.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The FY2026 impersonation-scams aggregate does not establish whether campaigns exploited protected age, disability or specific social/economic vulnerabilities, or identify the relevant Article 2 Union-market/deployer/output nexus. Investor loss alone does not establish the protected element, while absent victim-level detail cannot prove it absent.

review.reason_for_change: Article 5(1)(b) requires covered territorial AI use and the defined manipulation/vulnerability harm conditions. The Bronx scam or Australian public-figure scam reports do not establish Union scope. No EU prohibition finding is inferred from fraud reports.

review.requirement_proposition: Document interactions with GAI systems to users prior to interactive activities, particularly in contexts involving more significant risks.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: GV-5.1-002 concerns disclosure before interactive GAI activities. Static generated investment material and human scripted calls do not establish a recipient-side interactive GAI activity. Unpublished operator generation requests are a separate event, not substituted for this recipient pathway.

review.reason_for_change: GV-5.1-002 concerns information before or during interaction with AI. Victims viewed static advertisements and dealt with human scammers. No interaction with the generation system or autonomous AI interlocutor is established.

conclusion_change.previous: ASIC describes human scammers using generative AI, deepfake endorsements, fabricated news, fake social proof and fake investment platforms to create materially false investment premises and induce economic transfers. The classifiable mechanism is AI-mediated deceptive economic solicitation, alongside requester-side identity-authority failure; autonomous AI manipulation and hidden generator control states remain unproved. The regulator’s deliberate public-figure image misuse supports requester-side identity-authority failure independently of the economic and social-engineering findings. Aggregate reported losses and takedowns remain distinct quantities, without attribution to every named portrayal. Static ads and human scripted calls do not establish an autonomous AI interlocutor.
conclusion_change.new: ASIC describes human scammers using generative AI, deepfake endorsements, fabricated news, fake social proof and fake investment platforms to create materially false investment premises and induce economic transfers. The classifiable mechanism is AI-mediated deceptive economic solicitation, alongside requester-side identity-authority failure; autonomous AI manipulation and hidden generator control states remain unproved. The regulator’s deliberate public-figure image misuse supports requester-side identity-authority failure independently of the economic and social-engineering findings. Aggregate reported losses and takedowns remain distinct quantities, without attribution to every named portrayal. Static ads and human scripted calls do not establish an autonomous AI interlocutor. The independent dignity and autonomy assessment is Not aligned for the reported impersonation. Generator-specific controls are not established.
